title: add benchmark-lab profiling baselines and reporting pipeline v50
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds v50 profiling baselines, new representative workload runners, and updates the reporting pipeline to emit per-variant profiling metrics. No breaking API changes.
description:
Motivation: we need a fresh set of profiling baselines and improved reporting to capture multi-variant performance for recent runtime scheduler changes. This PR bundles three related changes: 1) profiling baselines for cold-start and steady-state across a set of representative workloads, 2) new representative workload runner harness that supports variable batch distributions and sequence-length histograms, and 3) reporting pipeline updates to ingest profiling artifacts and produce per-run and per-variant summaries for the benchmark dashboard.

Summary of changes: Added baseline datasets and harnesses under benchmark-lab/, introduced a new workload runner (representative_runner.py) that can replay production-like arrival patterns, extended the profiling pipeline job definitions in perf-canary/ci/ to capture KV-cache warmup metrics, and updated the reporting lambda to attach quantization/variant metadata. The change includes CI automation to run a subset of profiling workloads during nightly runs and a smoke test in PR CI.

Checklist:
- [x] Add profiling baseline definitions and sample inputs
- [x] Implement representative workload runner with configurable arrival distributions
- [x] Update reporting pipeline to accept and normalize profiling artifacts
- [x] Add CI smoke tests and nightly job configuration
- [x] Docs: add short README and usage examples for the new runner

Why now: recent scheduler changes (ENG-2759) introduced variance in cold-start latency for quantized variants; without per-variant profiling and reporting we cannot detect regressions before rollouts. This PR enables consistent profiling and end-to-end visibility in the dashboard so rollouts can be gated by quality and performance thresholds.

Notes on scope: this PR intentionally avoids changing runtime kernels or model weight configs. It only produces measurable baselines and the plumbing to get those baselines into the reporting pipeline. Future PRs will propose automated regression alerts and calibration runs.
